Completion of an appropriate undergraduate degree in computer science or a related discipline such as engineering, mathematics, or statistics.
Above-average academic track record, typically a cumulative grade point average of 1.7 or better after conversion to the German grading system
Studies must be closely related to SECAI research areas — e.g. M.Sc. Computer Science (TUD), M.Sc. Data Science (UL), or another program specialised towards an AI-related topic

Scholarship is aimed at students who intend to study AI or a related field at TU Dresden or Leipzig University; selection is mainly based on academic excellence, with attention to internationalisation and diversity

Open to applicants from all academic disciplines pursuing a postgraduate/Master's course of study in Germany; separate DAAD programmes apply for artistic disciplines and architecture (including Urban Design).
First degree (e.g. Bachelor's or Diplom) must be completed at the latest by the time the funding period begins.
The most recent university degree should generally not date back more than 6 years at the time of the application deadline.
Applicant must not have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
Applicants must intend to complete a Master's in mathematics, computer science, natural sciences or engineering at a German state or state-recognised university.
Applicants who already hold a Master's degree by the application deadline cannot apply.
Applicants cannot have been resident in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline.
Potential supervisor approval is not required before applying.
Open to domestic and international students; international MSc tuition rates are listed.
A pre-arranged supervisor is not required in order to apply; applicants may optionally list up to three preferred supervisors.
Minimum academic standard of an 'A−' or 80% average over the preceding two years of study

GRE General Test scores are encouraged but not required for applicants without a Canadian university degree.

Applications are evaluated in their totality: grades, statement of purpose, letters of reference and any supplementary information; admission is highly competitive (only 5-10% of applicants receive an offer).

Applicant must currently be, or soon will be, a Master-level student at TU Dresden or Leipzig University (applying in parallel to a Master's program is allowed, requiring two independent applications)
Applicant is responsible for obtaining admission to the chosen German university; admission must be submitted before the funding period begins.
Applicants must be high-achieving students from developing and emerging countries.
Applicants must have completed a first degree recognised in Germany by the application deadline.
Applicants must demonstrate above-average academic performance.
Applicants must choose a tuition-free Master's programme in Germany and secure admission before funding begins.
Applicants must be full-time research-stream graduate students in the Department of Computer Science (MSc or PhD).
Funding is conditional on satisfactory progress and guaranteed for a defined period (16 months for MSc).
All graduate students must apply for and accept external awards for which they are eligible.
Students in good academic standing must apply for the Departmental Fellowship by reporting external scholarships, stipends, and paid employment to the Graduate Office.
Recipients must report external financial awards valued at more than $10,000 CAD to the Graduate Office.
Must be in graduate studies at the master's or doctoral level
Must be enrolled full-time for 2 or more terms (21 to 52 weeks in total) in the academic year of application
Must attend one of the listed participating Ontario schools (e.g., University of Toronto, University of Waterloo, McMaster, Queen's)
Merit-based selection: application is assessed and ranked using criteria determined by the school you plan to attend
Must pursue graduate studies (master's, PhD or doctorate) in any non-professional graduate program at a university in Ontario, Canada
Awards go primarily to Canadian citizens, landed immigrants or permanent residents with preference for Ontario residents; 90 of 3,000 annual awards are reserved for temporary resident visa students
Recipient must attend a full-time graduate program in Ontario and may hold part-time employment of no more than 10 hours per week
Recipients may not simultaneously hold an OGS and a scholarship from SSHRC, NSERC, CIHR or an OGSST
The MSc in Computer Science is not open to international applicants; only domestic (Canadian) applicants are considered.
Standing equivalent to at least B+ (U of T 77-79% or 3.3/4.0) in the final year of full-time study.
Demonstrate English-language proficiency according to University of Toronto requirements.

Proof of proficiency in the language of instruction is required; for English-taught programmes certificates such as IELTS, TOEFL iBT, TOEFL Essentials, TOEIC, PTE Academic, Cambridge English or Duolingo English Test can be submitted.
Applicants must provide proof of at least CEFR B1 in the language of instruction; for English-taught programmes this can be shown with an accepted English test.
